Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 58, verse 1:

Tafsir of Surah al-Mujadila (The Pleading Woman)

It is Medinan.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

* *

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Tamim ibn Salama, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha, who said: "All praise is due to Allah, whose hearing encompasses all voices. The woman who pleaded (al-mujadila) came to the Prophet ﷺ speaking to him while I was in a corner of the house, not hearing what she said. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has heard the statement of she who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾ to the end of the verse." [[Al-Musnad (6/46).]]

Likewise, al-Bukhari narrated it in Kitab al-Tawhid as a suspended report (mu'allaq), saying: "And al-A'mash said, from Tamim ibn Salama, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha," and he mentioned it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7385).]] An-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir also narrated it through other routes, from al-A'mash, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11570); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (188); Tafsir al-Tabari (28/5).]]

In a narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, from al-A'mash, from Tamim ibn Salama, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha, that she said: "Blessed is He whose hearing takes in everything. I truly hear the speech of Khawla bint Tha'laba, and some of it is hidden from me, as she complains of her husband to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, my youth has been consumed by him, and I have given him my womb (through children), until when my age has advanced and my children have ceased, he has made me unlawful to himself (zihar). O Allah, I complain to You.'" She said: "She had not moved away before Jibril descended with this verse: ﴿Allah has heard the statement of she who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾." And her husband was Aws ibn al-Samit. [[In A: "wa-barat" (and she was exhausted) instead of "wa-nathart".]] [[In M: "wa-qalat" (and she said).]]

Ibn Lahi'a narrated, from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwa: "He is Aws ibn al-Samit, and Aws was a man afflicted with epilepsy (lamam). When his seizure took him and grew severe, he would make his wife unlawful to himself through zihar, and when it departed he would say nothing. She came to the Messenger of Allah seeking a ruling on this and complaining to Allah, so Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has heard the statement of she who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾ to the end of the verse."

Similarly, Hisham ibn 'Urwa narrated from his father that a man had epilepsy (lamam), and he mentioned a similar account.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il Abu Salama narrated to us, Jarir (meaning Ibn Hazim) narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Yazid narrate: A woman met 'Umar, who was walking with the people; she was called Khawla bint Tha'laba. She stopped him, and he stopped for her, drew near to her, bent his head to her, and placed his hands on her shoulders until she had finished her need and departed. A man said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, you have detained the notables of Quraysh for this old woman?!" He said: "Woe to you! Do you know who this is?" He said: "No." He said: "This is a woman whose complaint Allah heard from above the seven heavens. This is Khawla bint Tha'laba. By Allah, if she had not turned away from me until night, I would not have turned away from her until she had finished her need, unless a prayer came due, in which case I would pray it and then return to her until she had finished her need."

[[Narrated by al-Darimi in al-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyya (p. 26) by way of Abu Yazid, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. Al-Dhahabi said in al-'Uluw (p. 113): "This is a sound chain with a break, as Abu Yazid did not meet 'Umar."]]

This is a break (inqita') between Abu Yazid and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. It has been narrated by other routes as well.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us [[In A: "Al-Walid ibn al-Mundhir with Shadhan narrated to us."]] Ya'la narrated to us, Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Amir, who said: "The woman who pleaded concerning her husband was Khawla bint al-Samit, and her mother was Mu'adha, about whom Allah revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity﴾ [al-Nur: 33]."

The correct version: Khawla was the wife of Aws ibn al-Samit.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 58, verses 2–4 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Sa'd [[In A: "Sa'id".]] ibn Ibrahim and Ya'qub told us, both saying: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, Ma'mar ibn Abdullah ibn Handhalah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abdullah ibn Salam, on the authority of Khuwaylah [[In A: "Khawlah".]] bint Tha'labah, who said: "By Allah, it was about me and about Aws ibn al-Samit that Allah revealed the beginning of Surat al-Mujadilah." She said: "I was with him, and he was an old man whose temper had become bad. He came in to me one day and I argued with him about something, and he became angry and said: 'You are to me like the back of my mother.'" She said: "Then he went out and sat in the gathering of his people for a while, then he came back in to me and was trying to have his way with me." She said: "I said: 'No indeed, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Khuwaylah, you shall not come near me after what you have said, until Allah and His Messenger judge concerning us by His judgment.'" She said: "He pounced on me, but I resisted him, and I overpowered him with what a woman overpowers a weak old man with, and I threw him off me." She said: "Then I went out to one of my neighbour women and borrowed clothes from her, then I went out until I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I sat before him and told him what I had suffered from him, and I began to complain to him of the bad temper he had shown." She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began to say: 'O Khuwaylah, your cousin is an old man, so fear Allah concerning him.'" She said: "By Allah, I had not moved from my place before the Qur'an was revealed concerning me, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was overcome by what usually overcame him, then it passed from him, and he said to me: 'O Khuwaylah, Allah has revealed concerning you and your companion.'" Then he recited to me: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual discourse; indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾, up to His words: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾. She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'Tell him to free a slave.'" She said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, he does not have anything with which to free a slave.'" He said: "Then let him fast two consecutive months." She said: "I said: 'By Allah, he is an old man, he has no ability to fast.'" He said: "Then let him feed sixty poor persons, a wasq of dates." She said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, he does not have that either.'" She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Then we will help him with an 'araq of dates.'" She said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I will also help him with another 'araq.'" He said: "You have done well and have done good. Go and give charity on his behalf with it, then treat your cousin kindly."" She said: "So I did that."

Abu Dawud related it in the Book of Divorce in his Sunan by two routes, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, with the same wording [[Al-Musnad (6/410) and Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. (2214, 2215).]]. In his version the name is Khawlah bint Tha'labah, and it is also said of her: Khawlah bint Malik ibn Tha'labah. She may be diminutive, and it is said: Khuwaylah. There is no contradiction between these statements, as the matter here is close. And Allah knows best.

This is the sound position regarding the occasion of revelation of the beginning of this surah. As for the hadith of Salamah ibn Sakhr, it does not state that it was the occasion of revelation; rather, he was ordered to do what Allah revealed in this surah, namely freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding, as Imam Ahmad said:

Yazid ibn Harun told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata', on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, on the authority of Salamah ibn Sakhr al-Ansari, who said: "I was a man who had been given more of sexual desire for women than anyone else had been given. When Ramadan came, I made the zihar [[Zihar: the pre-Islamic formula of divorce by likening one's wife to one's mother's back.]] with my wife, until Ramadan should end, out of fear that I might have intercourse with her during the night, and then I would be continually doing so until the day overtook me, and I could not restrain myself." He said: "While she was serving me at night, a part of her body was revealed to me, so I pounced upon her. When morning came, I went to my people and told them my news, and I said: 'Come with me to the Prophet (ﷺ) so that I may inform him of my affair.' They said: 'No, by Allah, we will not do that; we fear that something will be revealed concerning us, or that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will say a saying about us whose shame will remain upon us. But go yourself and do whatever seems right to you.'" He said: "So I went out until I came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and I informed him of my affair. He said to me: 'Are you in this condition?' I said: 'I am in this condition.' He said: 'Are you in this condition?' I said: 'I am in this condition.' He said: 'Are you in this condition?' I said: 'Yes, here I am, so carry out upon me the judgment of Allah, the Exalted; I am patient with it.' He said: 'Free a slave.' He said: 'So I struck the side of my neck with my hand and said: "No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I do not own anything except it."' He said: 'Then fast two months.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, has what befell me befallen me except through fasting?' He said: 'Then give charity.' I said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, we spent this night of ours hungry, with no supper for us.' He said: 'Go to the official of the charity of Banu Zurayq, and say to him: let him give it to you, and feed from it on your behalf a wasq of dates to sixty poor persons, then use the rest for yourself and your dependants.'" He said: "So I returned to my people and said: 'I found among you narrowness and bad judgment, and I found with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ease and blessing. He has ordered that your charity be given to me, so give it to me.' So they gave it to me."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah related it in the same way, and al-Tirmidhi abridged it and graded it hasan [[Al-Musnad (4/37), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2213), Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2062), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3299).]].

The apparent context indicates that this story came after the story of Aws ibn al-Samit and his wife Khuwaylah bint Tha'labah, as the context of that and this indicates upon reflection.

Khasif said, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "The first person to make zihar from his wife was Aws ibn al-Samit, the brother of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, and his wife was Khawlah bint Tha'labah ibn Malik. When he made zihar from her, she feared that this would be a divorce, so she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Aws has made zihar from me, and if we separate we will be destroyed, and I have borne children from him, and I have spent my youth with him.' She was complaining of this and weeping, and nothing had yet come concerning this. So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾, up to His words: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned him and said: 'Are you able to find a slave to free?' He said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I am not able to.' He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered for him until he freed one on his behalf, and then he returned to his wife." Ibn Jarir related it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/6).]].

For this reason Ibn Abbas and most scholars adopted what we have stated, and Allah knows best.

As for His, the Exalted, words: ﴿Those of you who make zihar from their wives﴾: the origin of zihar is derived from "the back" (zahr). This is because in the Jahiliyyah, when one of them made zihar from his wife, he would say to her: "You are to me like the back of my mother." Then in the Shari'ah, zihar applied to the other limbs by analogy with the back. In the Jahiliyyah, zihar was a divorce, so Allah granted this Ummah a concession and made for it an expiation (kaffarah), and did not make it a divorce as they used to hold in their Jahiliyyah. Thus said more than one of the early generation (salaf).

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ubayd Allah ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: "In the Jahiliyyah, if a man said to his wife, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' she became forbidden to him. Then the first person to make zihar in Islam was Aws, and under him was a paternal cousin of his called Khuwaylah bint Tha'labah [[In A: "bint Khuwaylid", which is an error.]]. He made zihar from her, and he was struck with dismay and said: 'I do not see you except as having become forbidden to me.' She said to him the same thing. He said: 'Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So she came to the Messenger of Allah and found with him a woman who dresses hair, combing his head. He said: 'O Khuwaylah, we have not been commanded anything concerning your affair.' Then Allah revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ), and he said: 'O Khuwaylah, rejoice!' She said: 'Good.' He recited to her: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual discourse﴾, up to His words: ﴿And those who make zihar from their wives, then go back on what they said, then the freeing of a slave before they touch one another﴾."

She said: "What slave do we have? By Allah, he does not have a slave other than me." He said: ﴿Then whoever does not find, then fasting for two consecutive months﴾. She said: "By Allah, if it were not that he drinks three times a day, his sight would go!" He said: ﴿Then whoever is not able, then feeding sixty poor persons﴾. She said: "From where? It is only a meal to the next meal!" He said: He asked for half a wasq, thirty sa', and a wasq is sixty sa', and said: "Let him feed sixty poor persons, and let him return to you [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/3). Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad, no. (1076), Kashf al-Astar, by way of Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, and said: "We do not know it with this wording concerning zihar from the Prophet (ﷺ) except by this chain, and Abu Hamzah is weak in narration, and he opposed the reliable narrators in his narration and in the text of his hadith concerning the matter of zihar, because al-Zuhri related it on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and this chain — we know of no difference among the scholars of hadith regarding its soundness — and that the Prophet (ﷺ) called for a vessel containing fifteen sa'. The hadith of Abu Hamzah is munkar, and it contains a wording that indicates opposition to the Book, because he said: 'and let him return to you,' and she was his wife; so what is the meaning of his returning to his wife if he had not divorced her? This is something that is not permissible to be attributed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it only came from the narration of Abu Hamzah al-Thumali."]]." This is a good, strong chain and a strange wording. It has been related from Abu al-Aliyah something similar to this, and so Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 58, verses 2–4 (part 2 of 2):

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Harawi narrated to us: 'Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Khawlah bint Dulayj was married to a man from the Ansar. He was blind, poor, and of bad character. It was the divorce practice of the Jahiliyyah that when a man wanted to divorce his wife, he would say: "You are to me like the back of my mother" (anti 'alayya ka-zahri ummi). She had one or two children by him. One day she argued with him about something, and he said: "You are to me like the back of my mother." So she gathered her clothes around her and came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in the house of 'A'ishah, and 'A'ishah was washing one side of his head. She came before him with her children and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband is blind, poor, with nothing, and of bad character. I argued with him about something and he became angry and said, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and he did not intend divorce by it. I have one or two children by him." He said: "I know of you only that you have become forbidden to him." She said: "I complain to Allah of what has befallen me and of my children's fate." He said: 'A'ishah turned and washed the other side of his head, and she turned with him. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband is blind, poor, of bad character, and I have one or two children by him. I argued with him about something and he became angry and said, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and he did not intend divorce by it!" She said: He raised his head to me and said: "I know of you only that you have become forbidden to him." She said: "I complain to Allah of what has befallen me and of my children's fate?" He said: 'A'ishah saw the face of the Prophet ﷺ change, so she said to her: "Step back, step back!" So she withdrew. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in that state of revelation for as long as Allah willed. When the revelation ended, he said: "O 'A'ishah, where is the woman?" She was called, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Go and bring me your husband." She went hurrying and brought him. He was, as she had described, blind, poor, and of bad character. The Prophet ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of she who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾ up to His words ﴿And those who divorce [by zihar] from their wives and then wish to go back on what they said, [then the freeing of a slave]﴾." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you find a slave to free before you touch her?" He said: No. He said: "Can you fast two consecutive months?" He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, if I do not eat two or three times, my sight nearly fails." He said: "Can you feed sixty needy persons?" He said: "No, unless you help me." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ helped him and said: "Feed sixty needy persons." He said: And Allah transformed the divorce into zihar.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Abd al-A'la, from Dawud, who said: I heard Abu al-'Aliyah, and he related something similar, but more briefly than this context. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/3).]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The iila' (oath of abstention from intercourse) and the zihar were among the divorces of the Jahiliyyah. So Allah set the iila' at four months and made expiation (kaffarah) obligatory in zihar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in similar terms.

Imam Malik used the words ﴿from among you﴾ to argue that a disbeliever does not fall within this verse, since the address is to believers. The majority answered that this phrasing came in the usual manner, so it carries no implied restriction. The majority also cited the words ﴿from their wives﴾ to argue that a slave woman cannot be subject to zihar and does not fall within this address.

* *

As for His words ﴿They are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them﴾: meaning, a woman does not become a man's mother by his saying, "You are to me like my mother," or "like my mother," or "like the back of my mother," or anything similar. His mother is only the one who bore him. Therefore He said: ﴿And indeed they utter an objectionable word and falsehood﴾, meaning an ugly and false statement. ﴿And indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, meaning regarding what you did in the time of Jahiliyyah. Likewise, He pardons what slips from the tongue unintentionally, which the speaker did not mean. Abu Dawud narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard a man say to his wife, "O my sister," and he said: "Is she your sister?" This is a disapproval, but he did not make her forbidden to him by that alone, because he did not intend it. Had he intended it, she would have become forbidden to him, since according to the correct view there is no difference between the mother and the other prohibited relatives such as a sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, and similar. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2210), from the hadith of Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿And those who divorce by zihar from their wives and then wish to go back on what they said﴾: the early scholars and imams differed about the meaning of ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾. Some people said: the "return" is to repeat the word of zihar, saying it again. This view is false, and it was the preference of Ibn Hazm and the view of Dawud, and Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr related it from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, al-Farra', and a group of the theologians.

Al-Shafi'i said: it is that he keeps her after the zihar for a period in which he could have divorced her, but he does not divorce her.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: it is that he returns to intercourse or resolves upon it, and she is not lawful to him until he makes this expiation. It is related from Malik that it is the resolve to have intercourse or to keep her, and also from him that it is intercourse itself.

Abu Hanifah said: it is that he returns to zihar after its prohibition and after the removal of what the affair of the Jahiliyyah had been. So whenever a man makes zihar with his wife, he has made her forbidden by a prohibition that only expiation lifts. His companions and al-Layth ibn Sa'd followed this view.

Ibn Lahi'ah said: 'Ata' narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾: that is, they intend to return to the intercourse which they had forbidden to themselves.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it means touching in the private part. He saw no harm in having sensual contact short of intercourse before making expiation.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿before they touch one another﴾: that the touching (al-massu) means marital intercourse. 'Ata', al-Zuhri, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said likewise.

Al-Zuhri said: he is not permitted to kiss her or touch her until he makes expiation.

The people of the Sunan narrated from the hadith of 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I made zihar with my wife and then had intercourse with her before I made expiation." He said: "What led you to that, may Allah have mercy on you?" He said: "I saw her anklet in the light of the moon." He said: "Then do not approach her until you do what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan (2223), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan (1990), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (6/167), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan (2065).]]

Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan gharib sahih. [[In (m): "hasan sahih gharib".]] Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of 'Ikrimah as a mursal report (one whose chain omits a companion). Al-Nasa'i said: this is closer to the correct version. [[Sunan Abi Dawud (2221, 2222); Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/168).]]

* *

As for His words ﴿then freeing a slave﴾: meaning, freeing a complete slave before they touch one another. Here the word "slave" (raqabah) is unrestricted, not limited by faith, whereas in the expiation for killing it is restricted by faith. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, applied what is unrestricted here to what is restricted there, because the requirement is the same, namely freeing a slave. He supported this with what he related from Malik with his chain, from Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami, in the story of the black slave-girl, in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Free her, for she is a believer." Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and Muslim in his Sahih. [[al-Muwatta' (2/777), al-Musnad (5/447), and Sahih Muslim (537).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Yusuf [[In (a): "Yunus".]] ibn Musa narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I made zihar with my wife, then I had intercourse with her before I made expiation." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Did Allah not say ﴿before they touch one another﴾?" He said: "I was captivated by her." He said: "Refrain until you make expiation." [[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/204), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/386), through Isma'il ibn Muslim, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, similarly. al-Dhahabi said: "In its chain is Isma'il ibn Muslim, who is weak (wahin)."]]

Then al-Bazzar said: Nothing better is related from Ibn 'Abbas than this. Isma'il ibn Muslim has been criticized, but a large number of scholars narrated from him. The jurisprudential lesson in it is that the Prophet ﷺ ordered him only one expiation.

* *

As for His words ﴿That you may be admonished by it﴾: meaning, you are restrained by it. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾: meaning, He knows what sets you right, and He is Knowing of your conditions.

* *

As for His words ﴿So whoever does not find [a slave], then fasting two consecutive months before they touch one another. And whoever is unable, then feeding sixty needy persons﴾: the narrations about this have already preceded, in this order, as is established in the two Sahihs in the story of the man who had intercourse with his wife during Ramadan.

﴿That is that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾: meaning, We legislated this for this purpose.

* *

As for His words ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: meaning, His prohibitions, so do not violate them.

* *

As for His words ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾: meaning, those who do not believe and do not commit to the rulings of this law. Do not think that they are safe from affliction; no, the matter is not as they claim. Rather, for them is a painful punishment, meaning in this world and in the Hereafter.

She said: "I said: 'No indeed, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Khuwaylah, you shall not come near me after what you have said, until Allah and His Messenger judge concerning us by His judgment.'" She said: "He pounced on me, but I resisted him, and I overpowered him with what a woman overpowers a weak old man with, and I threw him off me." She said: "Then I went out to one of my neighbour women and borrowed clothes from her, then I went out until I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I sat before him and told him what I had suffered from him, and I began to complain to him of the bad temper he had shown." She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began to say: 'O Khuwaylah, your cousin is an old man, so fear Allah concerning him.'" She said: "By Allah, I had not moved from my place before the Qur'an was revealed concerning me, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was overcome by what usually overcame him, then it passed from him, and he said to me: 'O Khuwaylah, Allah has revealed concerning you and your companion.'" Then he recited to me: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual discourse; indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾, up to His words: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾. She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: 'Tell him to free a slave.'" She said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, he does not have anything with which to free a slave.'" He said: "Then let him fast two consecutive months." She said: "I said: 'By Allah, he is an old man, he has no ability to fast.'" He said: "Then let him feed sixty poor persons, a wasq of dates." She said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, he does not have that either.'" She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Then we will help him with an 'araq of dates.'" She said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I will also help him with another 'araq.'" He said: "You have done well and have done good. Go and give charity on his behalf with it, then treat your cousin kindly."" She said: "So I did that."

Abu Dawud related it in the Book of Divorce in his Sunan by two routes, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, with the same wording [[Al-Musnad (6/410) and Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. (2214, 2215).]]. In his version the name is Khawlah bint Tha'labah, and it is also said of her: Khawlah bint Malik ibn Tha'labah. She may be diminutive, and it is said: Khuwaylah. There is no contradiction between these statements, as the matter here is close. And Allah knows best.

This is the sound position regarding the occasion of revelation of the beginning of this surah. As for the hadith of Salamah ibn Sakhr, it does not state that it was the occasion of revelation; rather, he was ordered to do what Allah revealed in this surah, namely freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding, as Imam Ahmad said:

Yazid ibn Harun told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata', on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, on the authority of Salamah ibn Sakhr al-Ansari, who said: "I was a man who had been given more of sexual desire for women than anyone else had been given. When Ramadan came, I made the zihar [[Zihar: the pre-Islamic formula of divorce by likening one's wife to one's mother's back.]] with my wife, until Ramadan should end, out of fear that I might have intercourse with her during the night, and then I would be continually doing so until the day overtook me, and I could not restrain myself." He said: "While she was serving me at night, a part of her body was revealed to me, so I pounced upon her. When morning came, I went to my people and told them my news, and I said: 'Come with me to the Prophet (ﷺ) so that I may inform him of my affair.' They said: 'No, by Allah, we will not do that; we fear that something will be revealed concerning us, or that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will say a saying about us whose shame will remain upon us. But go yourself and do whatever seems right to you.'" He said: "So I went out until I came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and I informed him of my affair. He said to me: 'Are you in this condition?' I said: 'I am in this condition.' He said: 'Are you in this condition?' I said: 'I am in this condition.' He said: 'Are you in this condition?' I said: 'Yes, here I am, so carry out upon me the judgment of Allah, the Exalted; I am patient with it.' He said: 'Free a slave.' He said: 'So I struck the side of my neck with my hand and said: "No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I do not own anything except it."' He said: 'Then fast two months.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, has what befell me befallen me except through fasting?' He said: 'Then give charity.' I said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, we spent this night of ours hungry, with no supper for us.' He said: 'Go to the official of the charity of Banu Zurayq, and say to him: let him give it to you, and feed from it on your behalf a wasq of dates to sixty poor persons, then use the rest for yourself and your dependants.'" He said: "So I returned to my people and said: 'I found among you narrowness and bad judgment, and I found with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ease and blessing. He has ordered that your charity be given to me, so give it to me.' So they gave it to me."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah related it in the same way, and al-Tirmidhi abridged it and graded it hasan [[Al-Musnad (4/37), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2213), Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2062), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3299).]].

The apparent context indicates that this story came after the story of Aws ibn al-Samit and his wife Khuwaylah bint Tha'labah, as the context of that and this indicates upon reflection.

Khasif said, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "The first person to make zihar from his wife was Aws ibn al-Samit, the brother of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, and his wife was Khawlah bint Tha'labah ibn Malik. When he made zihar from her, she feared that this would be a divorce, so she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Aws has made zihar from me, and if we separate we will be destroyed, and I have borne children from him, and I have spent my youth with him.' She was complaining of this and weeping, and nothing had yet come concerning this. So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾, up to His words: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned him and said: 'Are you able to find a slave to free?' He said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I am not able to.' He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered for him until he freed one on his behalf, and then he returned to his wife." Ibn Jarir related it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/6).]].

For this reason Ibn Abbas and most scholars adopted what we have stated, and Allah knows best.

As for His, the Exalted, words: ﴿Those of you who make zihar from their wives﴾: the origin of zihar is derived from "the back" (zahr). This is because in the Jahiliyyah, when one of them made zihar from his wife, he would say to her: "You are to me like the back of my mother." Then in the Shari'ah, zihar applied to the other limbs by analogy with the back. In the Jahiliyyah, zihar was a divorce, so Allah granted this Ummah a concession and made for it an expiation (kaffarah), and did not make it a divorce as they used to hold in their Jahiliyyah. Thus said more than one of the early generation (salaf).

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ubayd Allah ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: "In the Jahiliyyah, if a man said to his wife, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' she became forbidden to him. Then the first person to make zihar in Islam was Aws, and under him was a paternal cousin of his called Khuwaylah bint Tha'labah [[In A: "bint Khuwaylid", which is an error.]]. He made zihar from her, and he was struck with dismay and said: 'I do not see you except as having become forbidden to me.' She said to him the same thing. He said: 'Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So she came to the Messenger of Allah and found with him a woman who dresses hair, combing his head. He said: 'O Khuwaylah, we have not been commanded anything concerning your affair.' Then Allah revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ), and he said: 'O Khuwaylah, rejoice!' She said: 'Good.' He recited to her: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual discourse﴾, up to His words: ﴿And those who make zihar from their wives, then go back on what they said, then the freeing of a slave before they touch one another﴾."

She said: "What slave do we have? By Allah, he does not have a slave other than me." He said: ﴿Then whoever does not find, then fasting for two consecutive months﴾. She said: "By Allah, if it were not that he drinks three times a day, his sight would go!" He said: ﴿Then whoever is not able, then feeding sixty poor persons﴾. She said: "From where? It is only a meal to the next meal!" He said: He asked for half a wasq, thirty sa', and a wasq is sixty sa', and said: "Let him feed sixty poor persons, and let him return to you [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/3). Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad, no. (1076), Kashf al-Astar, by way of Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, and said: "We do not know it with this wording concerning zihar from the Prophet (ﷺ) except by this chain, and Abu Hamzah is weak in narration, and he opposed the reliable narrators in his narration and in the text of his hadith concerning the matter of zihar, because al-Zuhri related it on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and this chain — we know of no difference among the scholars of hadith regarding its soundness — and that the Prophet (ﷺ) called for a vessel containing fifteen sa'. The hadith of Abu Hamzah is munkar, and it contains a wording that indicates opposition to the Book, because he said: 'and let him return to you,' and she was his wife; so what is the meaning of his returning to his wife if he had not divorced her? This is something that is not permissible to be attributed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it only came from the narration of Abu Hamzah al-Thumali."]]." This is a good, strong chain and a strange wording. It has been related from Abu al-Aliyah something similar to this, and so Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 58, verses 2–4 (part 2 of 2):

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Harawi narrated to us: 'Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Khawlah bint Dulayj was married to a man from the Ansar. He was blind, poor, and of bad character. It was the divorce practice of the Jahiliyyah that when a man wanted to divorce his wife, he would say: "You are to me like the back of my mother" (anti 'alayya ka-zahri ummi). She had one or two children by him. One day she argued with him about something, and he said: "You are to me like the back of my mother." So she gathered her clothes around her and came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in the house of 'A'ishah, and 'A'ishah was washing one side of his head. She came before him with her children and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband is blind, poor, with nothing, and of bad character. I argued with him about something and he became angry and said, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and he did not intend divorce by it. I have one or two children by him." He said: "I know of you only that you have become forbidden to him." She said: "I complain to Allah of what has befallen me and of my children's fate." He said: 'A'ishah turned and washed the other side of his head, and she turned with him. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband is blind, poor, of bad character, and I have one or two children by him. I argued with him about something and he became angry and said, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and he did not intend divorce by it!" She said: He raised his head to me and said: "I know of you only that you have become forbidden to him." She said: "I complain to Allah of what has befallen me and of my children's fate?" He said: 'A'ishah saw the face of the Prophet ﷺ change, so she said to her: "Step back, step back!" So she withdrew. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in that state of revelation for as long as Allah willed. When the revelation ended, he said: "O 'A'ishah, where is the woman?" She was called, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Go and bring me your husband." She went hurrying and brought him. He was, as she had described, blind, poor, and of bad character. The Prophet ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of she who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾ up to His words ﴿And those who divorce [by zihar] from their wives and then wish to go back on what they said, [then the freeing of a slave]﴾." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you find a slave to free before you touch her?" He said: No. He said: "Can you fast two consecutive months?" He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, if I do not eat two or three times, my sight nearly fails." He said: "Can you feed sixty needy persons?" He said: "No, unless you help me." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ helped him and said: "Feed sixty needy persons." He said: And Allah transformed the divorce into zihar.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Abd al-A'la, from Dawud, who said: I heard Abu al-'Aliyah, and he related something similar, but more briefly than this context. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/3).]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The iila' (oath of abstention from intercourse) and the zihar were among the divorces of the Jahiliyyah. So Allah set the iila' at four months and made expiation (kaffarah) obligatory in zihar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in similar terms.

Imam Malik used the words ﴿from among you﴾ to argue that a disbeliever does not fall within this verse, since the address is to believers. The majority answered that this phrasing came in the usual manner, so it carries no implied restriction. The majority also cited the words ﴿from their wives﴾ to argue that a slave woman cannot be subject to zihar and does not fall within this address.

* *

As for His words ﴿They are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them﴾: meaning, a woman does not become a man's mother by his saying, "You are to me like my mother," or "like my mother," or "like the back of my mother," or anything similar. His mother is only the one who bore him. Therefore He said: ﴿And indeed they utter an objectionable word and falsehood﴾, meaning an ugly and false statement. ﴿And indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, meaning regarding what you did in the time of Jahiliyyah. Likewise, He pardons what slips from the tongue unintentionally, which the speaker did not mean. Abu Dawud narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard a man say to his wife, "O my sister," and he said: "Is she your sister?" This is a disapproval, but he did not make her forbidden to him by that alone, because he did not intend it. Had he intended it, she would have become forbidden to him, since according to the correct view there is no difference between the mother and the other prohibited relatives such as a sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, and similar. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2210), from the hadith of Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿And those who divorce by zihar from their wives and then wish to go back on what they said﴾: the early scholars and imams differed about the meaning of ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾. Some people said: the "return" is to repeat the word of zihar, saying it again. This view is false, and it was the preference of Ibn Hazm and the view of Dawud, and Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr related it from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, al-Farra', and a group of the theologians.

Al-Shafi'i said: it is that he keeps her after the zihar for a period in which he could have divorced her, but he does not divorce her.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: it is that he returns to intercourse or resolves upon it, and she is not lawful to him until he makes this expiation. It is related from Malik that it is the resolve to have intercourse or to keep her, and also from him that it is intercourse itself.

Abu Hanifah said: it is that he returns to zihar after its prohibition and after the removal of what the affair of the Jahiliyyah had been. So whenever a man makes zihar with his wife, he has made her forbidden by a prohibition that only expiation lifts. His companions and al-Layth ibn Sa'd followed this view.

Ibn Lahi'ah said: 'Ata' narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾: that is, they intend to return to the intercourse which they had forbidden to themselves.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it means touching in the private part. He saw no harm in having sensual contact short of intercourse before making expiation.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿before they touch one another﴾: that the touching (al-massu) means marital intercourse. 'Ata', al-Zuhri, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said likewise.

Al-Zuhri said: he is not permitted to kiss her or touch her until he makes expiation.

The people of the Sunan narrated from the hadith of 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I made zihar with my wife and then had intercourse with her before I made expiation." He said: "What led you to that, may Allah have mercy on you?" He said: "I saw her anklet in the light of the moon." He said: "Then do not approach her until you do what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan (2223), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan (1990), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (6/167), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan (2065).]]

Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan gharib sahih. [[In (m): "hasan sahih gharib".]] Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of 'Ikrimah as a mursal report (one whose chain omits a companion). Al-Nasa'i said: this is closer to the correct version. [[Sunan Abi Dawud (2221, 2222); Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/168).]]

* *

As for His words ﴿then freeing a slave﴾: meaning, freeing a complete slave before they touch one another. Here the word "slave" (raqabah) is unrestricted, not limited by faith, whereas in the expiation for killing it is restricted by faith. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, applied what is unrestricted here to what is restricted there, because the requirement is the same, namely freeing a slave. He supported this with what he related from Malik with his chain, from Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami, in the story of the black slave-girl, in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Free her, for she is a believer." Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and Muslim in his Sahih. [[al-Muwatta' (2/777), al-Musnad (5/447), and Sahih Muslim (537).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Yusuf [[In (a): "Yunus".]] ibn Musa narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I made zihar with my wife, then I had intercourse with her before I made expiation." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Did Allah not say ﴿before they touch one another﴾?" He said: "I was captivated by her." He said: "Refrain until you make expiation." [[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/204), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/386), through Isma'il ibn Muslim, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, similarly. al-Dhahabi said: "In its chain is Isma'il ibn Muslim, who is weak (wahin)."]]

Then al-Bazzar said: Nothing better is related from Ibn 'Abbas than this. Isma'il ibn Muslim has been criticized, but a large number of scholars narrated from him. The jurisprudential lesson in it is that the Prophet ﷺ ordered him only one expiation.

* *

As for His words ﴿That you may be admonished by it﴾: meaning, you are restrained by it. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾: meaning, He knows what sets you right, and He is Knowing of your conditions.

* *

As for His words ﴿So whoever does not find [a slave], then fasting two consecutive months before they touch one another. And whoever is unable, then feeding sixty needy persons﴾: the narrations about this have already preceded, in this order, as is established in the two Sahihs in the story of the man who had intercourse with his wife during Ramadan.

﴿That is that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾: meaning, We legislated this for this purpose.

* *

As for His words ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: meaning, His prohibitions, so do not violate them.

* *

As for His words ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾: meaning, those who do not believe and do not commit to the rulings of this law. Do not think that they are safe from affliction; no, the matter is not as they claim. Rather, for them is a painful punishment, meaning in this world and in the Hereafter.

The apparent context indicates that this story came after the story of Aws ibn al-Samit and his wife Khuwaylah bint Tha'labah, as the context of that and this indicates upon reflection.

Khasif said, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "The first person to make zihar from his wife was Aws ibn al-Samit, the brother of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, and his wife was Khawlah bint Tha'labah ibn Malik. When he made zihar from her, she feared that this would be a divorce, so she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Aws has made zihar from me, and if we separate we will be destroyed, and I have borne children from him, and I have spent my youth with him.' She was complaining of this and weeping, and nothing had yet come concerning this. So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾, up to His words: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned him and said: 'Are you able to find a slave to free?' He said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I am not able to.' He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered for him until he freed one on his behalf, and then he returned to his wife." Ibn Jarir related it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/6).]].

For this reason Ibn Abbas and most scholars adopted what we have stated, and Allah knows best.

As for His, the Exalted, words: ﴿Those of you who make zihar from their wives﴾: the origin of zihar is derived from "the back" (zahr). This is because in the Jahiliyyah, when one of them made zihar from his wife, he would say to her: "You are to me like the back of my mother." Then in the Shari'ah, zihar applied to the other limbs by analogy with the back. In the Jahiliyyah, zihar was a divorce, so Allah granted this Ummah a concession and made for it an expiation (kaffarah), and did not make it a divorce as they used to hold in their Jahiliyyah. Thus said more than one of the early generation (salaf).

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ubayd Allah ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: "In the Jahiliyyah, if a man said to his wife, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' she became forbidden to him. Then the first person to make zihar in Islam was Aws, and under him was a paternal cousin of his called Khuwaylah bint Tha'labah [[In A: "bint Khuwaylid", which is an error.]]. He made zihar from her, and he was struck with dismay and said: 'I do not see you except as having become forbidden to me.' She said to him the same thing. He said: 'Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So she came to the Messenger of Allah and found with him a woman who dresses hair, combing his head. He said: 'O Khuwaylah, we have not been commanded anything concerning your affair.' Then Allah revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ), and he said: 'O Khuwaylah, rejoice!' She said: 'Good.' He recited to her: ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of her who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual discourse﴾, up to His words: ﴿And those who make zihar from their wives, then go back on what they said, then the freeing of a slave before they touch one another﴾."

She said: "What slave do we have? By Allah, he does not have a slave other than me." He said: ﴿Then whoever does not find, then fasting for two consecutive months﴾. She said: "By Allah, if it were not that he drinks three times a day, his sight would go!" He said: ﴿Then whoever is not able, then feeding sixty poor persons﴾. She said: "From where? It is only a meal to the next meal!" He said: He asked for half a wasq, thirty sa', and a wasq is sixty sa', and said: "Let him feed sixty poor persons, and let him return to you [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/3). Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad, no. (1076), Kashf al-Astar, by way of Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, and said: "We do not know it with this wording concerning zihar from the Prophet (ﷺ) except by this chain, and Abu Hamzah is weak in narration, and he opposed the reliable narrators in his narration and in the text of his hadith concerning the matter of zihar, because al-Zuhri related it on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and this chain — we know of no difference among the scholars of hadith regarding its soundness — and that the Prophet (ﷺ) called for a vessel containing fifteen sa'. The hadith of Abu Hamzah is munkar, and it contains a wording that indicates opposition to the Book, because he said: 'and let him return to you,' and she was his wife; so what is the meaning of his returning to his wife if he had not divorced her? This is something that is not permissible to be attributed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it only came from the narration of Abu Hamzah al-Thumali."]]." This is a good, strong chain and a strange wording. It has been related from Abu al-Aliyah something similar to this, and so Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 58, verses 2–4 (part 2 of 2):

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Harawi narrated to us: 'Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Khawlah bint Dulayj was married to a man from the Ansar. He was blind, poor, and of bad character. It was the divorce practice of the Jahiliyyah that when a man wanted to divorce his wife, he would say: "You are to me like the back of my mother" (anti 'alayya ka-zahri ummi). She had one or two children by him. One day she argued with him about something, and he said: "You are to me like the back of my mother." So she gathered her clothes around her and came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in the house of 'A'ishah, and 'A'ishah was washing one side of his head. She came before him with her children and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband is blind, poor, with nothing, and of bad character. I argued with him about something and he became angry and said, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and he did not intend divorce by it. I have one or two children by him." He said: "I know of you only that you have become forbidden to him." She said: "I complain to Allah of what has befallen me and of my children's fate." He said: 'A'ishah turned and washed the other side of his head, and she turned with him. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband is blind, poor, of bad character, and I have one or two children by him. I argued with him about something and he became angry and said, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' and he did not intend divorce by it!" She said: He raised his head to me and said: "I know of you only that you have become forbidden to him." She said: "I complain to Allah of what has befallen me and of my children's fate?" He said: 'A'ishah saw the face of the Prophet ﷺ change, so she said to her: "Step back, step back!" So she withdrew. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in that state of revelation for as long as Allah willed. When the revelation ended, he said: "O 'A'ishah, where is the woman?" She was called, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Go and bring me your husband." She went hurrying and brought him. He was, as she had described, blind, poor, and of bad character. The Prophet ﷺ said: "I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Allah has indeed heard the speech of she who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾ up to His words ﴿And those who divorce [by zihar] from their wives and then wish to go back on what they said, [then the freeing of a slave]﴾." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you find a slave to free before you touch her?" He said: No. He said: "Can you fast two consecutive months?" He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, if I do not eat two or three times, my sight nearly fails." He said: "Can you feed sixty needy persons?" He said: "No, unless you help me." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ helped him and said: "Feed sixty needy persons." He said: And Allah transformed the divorce into zihar.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Abd al-A'la, from Dawud, who said: I heard Abu al-'Aliyah, and he related something similar, but more briefly than this context. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/3).]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The iila' (oath of abstention from intercourse) and the zihar were among the divorces of the Jahiliyyah. So Allah set the iila' at four months and made expiation (kaffarah) obligatory in zihar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in similar terms.

Imam Malik used the words ﴿from among you﴾ to argue that a disbeliever does not fall within this verse, since the address is to believers. The majority answered that this phrasing came in the usual manner, so it carries no implied restriction. The majority also cited the words ﴿from their wives﴾ to argue that a slave woman cannot be subject to zihar and does not fall within this address.

* *

As for His words ﴿They are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them﴾: meaning, a woman does not become a man's mother by his saying, "You are to me like my mother," or "like my mother," or "like the back of my mother," or anything similar. His mother is only the one who bore him. Therefore He said: ﴿And indeed they utter an objectionable word and falsehood﴾, meaning an ugly and false statement. ﴿And indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, meaning regarding what you did in the time of Jahiliyyah. Likewise, He pardons what slips from the tongue unintentionally, which the speaker did not mean. Abu Dawud narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard a man say to his wife, "O my sister," and he said: "Is she your sister?" This is a disapproval, but he did not make her forbidden to him by that alone, because he did not intend it. Had he intended it, she would have become forbidden to him, since according to the correct view there is no difference between the mother and the other prohibited relatives such as a sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, and similar. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2210), from the hadith of Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿And those who divorce by zihar from their wives and then wish to go back on what they said﴾: the early scholars and imams differed about the meaning of ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾. Some people said: the "return" is to repeat the word of zihar, saying it again. This view is false, and it was the preference of Ibn Hazm and the view of Dawud, and Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr related it from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, al-Farra', and a group of the theologians.

Al-Shafi'i said: it is that he keeps her after the zihar for a period in which he could have divorced her, but he does not divorce her.

Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: it is that he returns to intercourse or resolves upon it, and she is not lawful to him until he makes this expiation. It is related from Malik that it is the resolve to have intercourse or to keep her, and also from him that it is intercourse itself.

Abu Hanifah said: it is that he returns to zihar after its prohibition and after the removal of what the affair of the Jahiliyyah had been. So whenever a man makes zihar with his wife, he has made her forbidden by a prohibition that only expiation lifts. His companions and al-Layth ibn Sa'd followed this view.

Ibn Lahi'ah said: 'Ata' narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿then wish to go back on what they said﴾: that is, they intend to return to the intercourse which they had forbidden to themselves.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it means touching in the private part. He saw no harm in having sensual contact short of intercourse before making expiation.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿before they touch one another﴾: that the touching (al-massu) means marital intercourse. 'Ata', al-Zuhri, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said likewise.

Al-Zuhri said: he is not permitted to kiss her or touch her until he makes expiation.

The people of the Sunan narrated from the hadith of 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I made zihar with my wife and then had intercourse with her before I made expiation." He said: "What led you to that, may Allah have mercy on you?" He said: "I saw her anklet in the light of the moon." He said: "Then do not approach her until you do what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded you." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan (2223), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan (1990), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (6/167), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan (2065).]]

Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan gharib sahih. [[In (m): "hasan sahih gharib".]] Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of 'Ikrimah as a mursal report (one whose chain omits a companion). Al-Nasa'i said: this is closer to the correct version. [[Sunan Abi Dawud (2221, 2222); Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/168).]]

* *

As for His words ﴿then freeing a slave﴾: meaning, freeing a complete slave before they touch one another. Here the word "slave" (raqabah) is unrestricted, not limited by faith, whereas in the expiation for killing it is restricted by faith. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, applied what is unrestricted here to what is restricted there, because the requirement is the same, namely freeing a slave. He supported this with what he related from Malik with his chain, from Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami, in the story of the black slave-girl, in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Free her, for she is a believer." Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and Muslim in his Sahih. [[al-Muwatta' (2/777), al-Musnad (5/447), and Sahih Muslim (537).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Yusuf [[In (a): "Yunus".]] ibn Musa narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I made zihar with my wife, then I had intercourse with her before I made expiation." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Did Allah not say ﴿before they touch one another﴾?" He said: "I was captivated by her." He said: "Refrain until you make expiation." [[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/204), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/386), through Isma'il ibn Muslim, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, similarly. al-Dhahabi said: "In its chain is Isma'il ibn Muslim, who is weak (wahin)."]]

Then al-Bazzar said: Nothing better is related from Ibn 'Abbas than this. Isma'il ibn Muslim has been criticized, but a large number of scholars narrated from him. The jurisprudential lesson in it is that the Prophet ﷺ ordered him only one expiation.

* *

As for His words ﴿That you may be admonished by it﴾: meaning, you are restrained by it. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾: meaning, He knows what sets you right, and He is Knowing of your conditions.

* *

As for His words ﴿So whoever does not find [a slave], then fasting two consecutive months before they touch one another. And whoever is unable, then feeding sixty needy persons﴾: the narrations about this have already preceded, in this order, as is established in the two Sahihs in the story of the man who had intercourse with his wife during Ramadan.

﴿That is that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾: meaning, We legislated this for this purpose.

* *

As for His words ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: meaning, His prohibitions, so do not violate them.

* *

As for His words ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾: meaning, those who do not believe and do not commit to the rulings of this law. Do not think that they are safe from affliction; no, the matter is not as they claim. Rather, for them is a painful punishment, meaning in this world and in the Hereafter.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, exalted is He, informs about those who opposed Allah and His Messenger and defied His law: ﴿They will be disgraced as those before them were disgraced﴾, meaning they will be humiliated, cursed and abased, just as those of their kind before them were treated. ﴿And We have sent down clear signs﴾, meaning manifest ones, which none opposes or defiantly rejects except a disbelieving, wicked and arrogant person. ﴿And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment﴾, meaning in return for their arrogance in refusing to follow the law of Allah, to submit to it, and to humble themselves before it.

Then He said: ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all together﴾, and that is the Day of Resurrection, when Allah will gather the first and the last in one place. ﴿And He will inform them of what they did﴾, meaning He will inform them of what they had done of good and evil. ﴿Allah has enumerated it, and they have forgotten it﴾, meaning Allah has recorded it and preserved it against them, while they themselves have forgotten what they were doing. ﴿And Allah is Witness over all things﴾, meaning nothing is hidden from Him, and He neither forgets nor overlooks anything.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, informing about the encompassing of His knowledge of His creation, His awareness of them, His hearing of their speech, and His seeing of their whereabouts wherever and wherever they may be: ﴿Have you not considered that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? There is no secret conversation among three but that He is their fourth, nor among five but that He is their sixth, nor among fewer than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are.﴾ Meaning: He is aware of them, hears their speech, their secrets and their private conversations. His messengers also, along with that, record what they confide, alongside Allah's knowledge and His hearing of them, as He said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private conversation, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾ [At-Tawbah: 78] And He said: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 80]. For this reason, more than one scholar has related the consensus (ijma') that the meaning of this verse is the accompaniment of Allah's knowledge, exalted is He. There is no doubt that this is intended, but His hearing is also, along with His knowledge, encompassing them, and His sight penetrates them. Thus He, glorified is He, is aware of His creation, and nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him.

Then He said: ﴿Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ Imam Ahmad said: "He began the verse with knowledge and concluded it with knowledge."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 58, verses 8–10:

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Have you not considered those who were forbidden from secret counsel (al-najwa)?﴾: "They are the Jews." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same, and added: "There was a truce (muwada'ah) between the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Jews. Whenever a man from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by them, they would sit and hold secret conversations among themselves, so that the believer would think they were conspiring to kill him, or to do something else the believer would dislike. When the believer saw this, he became fearful and turned away from their path. The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade them from secret counsel, but they did not desist and returned to their secret counsel. So Allah revealed: ﴿Have you not considered those who were forbidden from secret counsel, and then return to what they were forbidden?﴾"

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Hamzah narrated to me, from Kathir, from Zayd, from Rubayh ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "We would take turns to be with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). We would spend the night with him when some matter came to him at night or when he had some need. One night, the people on duty and those who had come to seek reward grew numerous, until we were in groups talking. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and said: 'What is this secret counsel? Were you not forbidden from secret counsel?' We said: 'We repent to Allah, O Messenger of Allah. We were speaking about the Messiah (al-Masih), and we were afraid of him.' He said: 'Shall I not tell you about something that I fear for you more than that?' We said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Hidden shirk: that a man stands up to perform an act so that another man may see him.'" This is a gharib (rare) chain, and it contains some weak narrators. [Footnote: Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (3/30) and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 4204, through Kathir ibn Zayd with similar wording. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/296): "This is a hasan chain; Kathir ibn Zayd and Rubayh ibn Abd al-Rahman are disputed."]

* *

As for His words ﴿and they hold secret counsel in sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger﴾: that is, they talk among themselves about sin (al-ithm), which concerns only themselves, and transgression ('udwan), which concerns others. Among it is disobedience to the Messenger and opposition to him. They persist in it and urge one another to it.

* *

As for His words ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with a greeting with which Allah has not greeted you﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, [from Muslim] [Insertion from al-Musnad (6/229)], from Masruq, from A'ishah, who said: "Some Jews entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'As-sam 'alayka, O Abu al-Qasim' (death be upon you). A'ishah said: 'And upon you be as-sam and [the curse]' [Insertion from A]. She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O A'ishah, Allah does not love obscenity or the use of obscene speech.' I said: 'Do you not hear them saying as-sam 'alayka?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Did you not hear me say: wa 'alaykum (and upon you)?' So Allah revealed: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with a greeting with which Allah has not greeted you﴾." [Footnote: Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, no. 2165, through Ya'la ibn Ubayd, from al-A'mash, with similar wording.]

In a narration in the Sahih, she said to them: "Upon you be as-sam, and al-dham (reproach), and the curse."
