Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse was revealed on a Friday, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at that time in the Suffah, and the place was cramped. He used to honour the people of Badr from among the Muhajirun and the Ansar. Some people from among the people of Badr came, and they had arrived at the gatherings first, so they stood in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings." The Prophet ﷺ returned the greeting. Then they greeted the people (present) after that, and they returned their greeting, but they stood on their feet waiting for room to be made for them. The Prophet ﷺ understood what was prompting them to stand, but no room was made for them, and this grieved the Prophet ﷺ. So he said to those around him from among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, who were not of the people of Badr: "Stand up, so-and-so, and you, so-and-so." He continued to make them stand, according to the number of the men who were standing before him from among the Muhajirun and the Ansar who were of the people of Badr. This grieved those who were made to rise from their seats, and the Prophet ﷺ noticed the dislike in their faces. The hypocrites said: "Do you not claim that this companion of yours is just among the people? By Allah, we have not seen him be just to these people. A group took their seats and loved to be close to their Prophet, so he made them rise and seated those who were slow to come to him." It reached us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who makes room for his brother." Thereafter they began to rise quickly, and the people made room for their brothers, and this verse was revealed on Friday. Related by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Imam Ahmad and al-Shafi'i said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man should not make another man rise from his place and then sit in it; rather, make room and widen (the space)."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Nafi', with the same wording.

[[This hadith did not occur to me in the Musnad of Ahmad in this form; rather it is in it (2/22): from Ibn Numayr, from Ubaydullah ibn Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar; (2/45) from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar. It is in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6269), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2177).]]

Al-Shafi'i said: Abd al-Majid informed us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Sulayman ibn Musa said, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you should make his brother rise on Friday, but rather let him say: 'Make room.'" It is on the condition of the Sunan (collections), but they did not record it.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Malik ibn Amr narrated to us, Fulayh narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn [Abi] Sa'sa'ah, from Ya'qub ibn Abi Ya'qub, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "A man should not make another man rise from his place and then sit in it; rather, make room, and Allah will make room for you."

He also narrated it from Suraij ibn Yunus and Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, from Fulayh, with the wording: "A man should not stand up for another man from his seat, but rather make room, and Allah will make room for you." Ahmad alone narrated it.

The jurists have differed concerning the permissibility of standing up for one who arrives, in several opinions. Among them are those who permitted it, citing the hadith: "Stand up for your master (qumu ila sayyidikum)." [[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (3043), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1768), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Among them are those who forbade it, citing the hadith: "Whoever loves that men should stand before him, let him take his seat in the Fire." [[Related by Abu Dawud in the Sunan, no. (5229), and al-Tirmidhi in the Sunan, no. (2755), from the hadith of Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him; al-Tirmidhi said: "Its isnad is hasan."]] Among them are those who made a distinction and said: it is permissible upon arrival from a journey, and for a judge within the area of his jurisdiction, as indicated by the story of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, for when the Prophet ﷺ summoned him to judge the Banu Qurayzah and he saw him approaching, he said to the Muslims: "Stand up for your master." That was only so that his ruling would be more binding, and Allah knows best. As for making it a habit, it is a custom of the non-Arabs (ajam). It has come in the Sunan that there was no person more beloved to them than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, yet when he came they did not stand for him, because they knew that he disliked that. [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in the Sunan, no. (2754), from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]] [[Imam al-Nawawi, may Allah have mercy on him, has a treatise titled: "Al-Tarkhis bil-qiyam li-dhawi al-fadl wal-muzayyah min ahl al-Islam" (The Permission to Stand for People of Virtue and Distinction among the Muslims), in which he elaborated extensively on this question; it is published by Dar al-Fikr in Damascus.]]

In the hadith narrated in the Sunan: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sit wherever the gathering ended, but wherever he sat, that became the head of that gathering. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, used to sit before him according to their ranks: Abu Bakr would seat him on his right, and Umar on his left, and in front of him generally were Uthman and Ali, because they were among those who wrote down the revelation, and he used to command them to do so, as Muslim narrated from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Umarah ibn Umayr, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abu Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "Let those of you who have wisdom and understanding stand closest to me, then those who come after them, then those who come after them." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (432).]] This was only so that they might understand what he said, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. For this reason he ordered those men to stand so that those who arrived from the people of Badr could sit, either because of those men's shortcoming in regard to the rights of the people of Badr, or so that the people of Badr might take their share of knowledge, as those before them had taken, or as a teaching for placing the excellent at the front.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Umarah ibn Umayr al-Taymi [in A: "al-Laythi"], from Abu Ma'mar, from Abu Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to straighten our shoulders in prayer and say: "Stand straight and do not differ, lest your hearts differ. Let those of you who have wisdom and understanding stand closest to me, then those who come after them, then those who come after them." Abu Mas'ud said: "So you today are far more divided."

Likewise Muslim and the authors of the Sunan (except al-Tirmidhi) narrated it through several chains from al-A'mash, with the same wording.

And if this was his command to them in prayer, that those of wisdom and then the scholars should stand closest to him, then it is all the more fitting that this should apply outside prayer.

Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Straighten the rows, align the shoulders, fill the gaps, be gentle with the hands of your brothers, and do not leave openings for Shaytan. Whoever joins a row, Allah will join him; and whoever cuts off a row, Allah will cut him off." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (666).]] For this reason Ubayy ibn Ka'b, the master of the reciters, when he reached the first row, would pull a man from it who was of the common people, and enter the front row himself, citing this hadith: "Let those of you who have wisdom and understanding stand closest to me." As for Abdullah ibn Umar, he would not sit in a place from which his companion had been made to rise, acting upon what he had transmitted of the hadith we have cited.

Let us be content with this measure of the model concerning this verse; otherwise its full exposition would require a place other than this one. And in the authentic hadith: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting, three men came. One of them found an opening in the circle and entered it; the second sat behind the people; and the third turned away and left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you about the three? As for the first, he sought refuge with Allah, so Allah sheltered him; as for the second, he was shy, so Allah was shy of him; and as for the third, he turned away, so Allah turned away from him." [[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (66), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2176).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Attab ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Abdullah informed us, Usamah ibn Zayd informed us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Amr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is not lawful for a man to separate two people except with their permission."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd al-Laythi, with the same wording. [[Musnad (2/213); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4845); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2752).]] And al-Tirmidhi graded it hasan.

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan al-Basri and others that they said concerning His saying: ﴿When you are told, "Make room in the assembly, then make room"﴾, that it means: in the assemblies of war. They said: and the meaning of His saying ﴿and when you are told, "Rise up, then rise"﴾ is: stand up for fighting.

Qatadah said: ﴿And when you are told, "Rise up, then rise"﴾ means: when you are called to good, respond.

Muqatil [ibn Hayyan] [addition from M] said: when you are called to prayer, rise up to it.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: When they were with the Prophet ﷺ in his house and wished to depart, each one loved to be the last of them to leave from his presence, and sometimes that would burden him, peace be upon him, and he might have a need. So they were commanded that when they are told to depart, they should depart, as in His saying: ﴿And if you are told, "Return," then return﴾ [An-Nur: 28]. [[In M: "And if it is said, return" which is an error.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah will raise those of you who have believed and those who were given knowledge by degrees, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, meaning: do not believe that if one of you makes room for his brother when he approaches, or rises when he is told to leave and leaves, that this is a diminution of his standing; rather, it is an elevation and a distinction in the sight of Allah. Allah the Exalted does not waste that for him; rather He will reward him for it in this world and the Hereafter, for whoever humbles himself before the command of Allah, Allah raises his rank and spreads his remembrance. For this reason He said: ﴿Allah will raise those of you who have believed and those who were given knowledge by degrees, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾.

That is: He is Acquainted with who deserves that and with who does not deserve it.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Kamil narrated to us, Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from Abu al-Tufayl Amir ibn Wathila, that Nafi' ibn Abd al-Harith met Umar ibn al-Khattab at Usfan, and Umar had appointed him over Makkah. Umar said to him: "Whom did you appoint over the people of the valley?" He said: "I appointed over them Ibn Abza." He said: "And who is Ibn Abza?" He said: "A man from among our clients (mawali)." Umar [ibn al-Khattab] [[Addition from M.]] said: "You appointed over them a client?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, he is a reciter of the Book of Allah, knowledgeable in the laws of inheritance (al-fara'id), and a judge." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Indeed, your Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah raises by this Book a people and lowers others by it.'" [[Al-Musnad (1/35).]]

Similarly, Muslim narrated it through more than one chain, from al-Zuhri, with the same wording. [[Coming through Hammad ibn Salamah from Humayd, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim: that Umar appointed Ibn Abd al-Harith over Makkah, and he mentioned something similar; recorded by Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (1/185), and it contains a break in the chain (inqita'). Also through al-A'mash from Habib ibn Abi Thabit: that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla said: "I went out with Umar, and we met the governor of Makkah, Nafi' ibn Alqama," and he mentioned something similar to the earlier hadith; recorded by Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (1/186).]] I have already mentioned the virtue of knowledge and its people, and the hadiths related on this subject, in detail in the commentary on the "Book of Knowledge" from Sahih al-Bukhari, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants: when one of them wishes to consult the Messenger of Allah ﷺ privately (i.e., to speak with him in secret between himself and him), he should first give a charity (ṣadaqah) before that. It purifies him, cleanses him and qualifies him to be fit for this station. For this reason He said: ﴿That is better for you and purer﴾ [[In A: "dhalikum", which is an error]].

Then He said: ﴿But if you do not find [anything]﴾, i.e., except for one who is unable to do so due to having nothing, ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. So He only commanded it of those who were able to do it.

Then He said: ﴿Are you apprehensive about offering charity before your private consultation?﴾ i.e., were you afraid of the continuation of this ruling upon you, namely the obligation of giving charity before consulting the Messenger? ﴿So when you do not do it and Allah has forgiven you, then establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

So the obligation of that was abrogated (naskh) for them.

It has been said that no one acted upon this verse before its abrogation except ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him.

Ibn Abī Najīḥ said, from Mujāhid, who said: They were forbidden from privately consulting the Prophet ﷺ until they gave charity, so none consulted him except ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who offered a dinar as charity, then consulted the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about ten matters. Then the concession was revealed.

Layth ibn Abī Sulaym said, from Mujāhid, who said: ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "There is a verse in the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic, that no one acted upon before me and no one will act upon after me. I had a dinar, which I exchanged for ten dirhams, and whenever I consulted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I gave a dirham in charity. Then it was abrogated, and no one acted upon it before me, nor will anyone act upon it after me." Then he recited this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger, present before your consultation a charity﴾ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Jarīr said: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿUthmān ibn al-Mughīrah, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAlqamah al-Anmārī, from ʿAlī [ibn Abī Ṭālib] – may Allah be pleased with him – who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "What do you think, a dinar?" He said: They cannot manage it. He said: "Half a dinar?" He said: They cannot manage it. He said: "What do you think?" He said: "A barley grain." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Indeed, you are frugal [[In M and A: "Innaka la-zahid"]]." He said: ʿAlī said: "Because of me, Allah lightened this for this Ummah, and His saying: ﴿[O you who have believed] [[Addition from M.]] when you consult the Messenger, present before your consultation a charity﴾ — then this was revealed: ﴿Are you apprehensive about offering charity before your private consultation?﴾" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/15); ʿAlī ibn ʿAlqamah has weakness in him. Al-Bukhari said: "There is something to examine in his narration."]]

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ, from Yaḥyā ibn Ādam, from ʿUbayd Allah al-Ashjaʿī, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from ʿUthmān ibn al-Mughīrah al-Thaqafī, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAlqamah al-Anmārī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger, present before your consultation a charity﴾ [to its end], the Prophet ﷺ said to me: "What do you think, a dinar?" I said: They cannot manage it. He mentioned it in full, similarly, then said: "This is a ḥasan gharīb ḥadīth; we only know it through this route." Then he said: As for the meaning of his saying "a barley grain": that is the weight of a barley grain of gold. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3300.]]

Abu Yaʿlā also narrated it, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yaḥyā ibn Ādam, with the same chain. [[Musnad Abi Yaʿla (1/322).]]

Al-ʿAwfī said, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger, present before your consultation a charity﴾ up to ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: the Muslims used to give charity before private consultation, then when zakah was revealed, this was abrogated.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah said, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿So present before your consultation a charity﴾: this was because the Muslims asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ too many questions until they burdened him, so Allah wished to lighten the burden on His Prophet, peace be upon him. When He said that, many of the people refrained and stopped asking, so Allah revealed after this: ﴿Are you apprehensive about offering charity before your private consultation? [[(1,2) In A: "ṣadaqāt".]] So when you do not do it and Allah has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakah﴾. So Allah widened the matter for them and did not constrict it.

ʿIkrimah and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said regarding His saying: ﴿So present before your consultation a charity﴾: it was abrogated by the verse that follows it, ﴿Are you apprehensive about offering charity before your private consultation? [[(1,2) In A: "ṣadaqāt".]]﴾ to its end.

Saʿīd [ibn Abī ʿArūbah] [[Addition from M, A.]] said, from Qatādah and Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān: The people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so much, until they wearied him with questions, so Allah cut them off with this verse. Thereafter, whenever one of them had a need of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, he could not fulfill it until he offered a charity before it. This was hard on them, so Allah revealed the concession after that: ﴿But if you do not find [anything], then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ma'mar said, from Qatādah: ﴿When you consult the Messenger, present before your consultation a charity﴾ — it is abrogated; it lasted only an hour of a day. And likewise ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Mujāhid, who said: ʿAlī said: "No one acted upon it except me until it was abrogated," and I think he also said: "And it lasted only an hour."

Allah, the Exalted, says, rebuking the hypocrites for their allegiance in secret to the disbelievers, while in reality they are neither with them nor with the believers, as Allah says: ﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whoever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way﴾ [An-Nisa 4:143]. Here He says: ﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah is angry?﴾ meaning the Jews, whom the hypocrites used to flatter and befriend in secret. Then He says: ﴿They are neither of you nor of them﴾, meaning these hypocrites are in truth neither of you, O believers, nor of those they befriended, namely the Jews.

Then He says: ﴿And they swear by Allah to a lie, while they know﴾, meaning the hypocrites swear falsely while knowing that they are lying in what they swear to. This is the yamin al-ghamus (the false oath that plunges its swearer into sin), especially given their cursed state. We seek refuge with Allah from that [[In M: "We seek refuge with Allah from that."]]. When they met the believers, they said, "We believe," and when they came to the Messenger, they swore by Allah [to him] [[Addition from M.]] that they were believers, while knowing that they were lying in what they swore, because they did not believe in the truth of what they said, even if it happened to correspond with reality. And whoever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way﴾ [An-Nisa 4:143]. Here He says: ﴿Have you not considered those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah is angry?﴾ meaning the Jews, whom the hypocrites used to flatter and befriend in secret. Then He says: ﴿They are neither of you nor of them﴾, meaning these hypocrites are in truth neither of you, O believers, nor of those they befriended, namely the Jews.

Then He says: ﴿And they swear by Allah to a lie, while they know﴾, meaning the hypocrites swear falsely while knowing that they are lying in what they swear to. This is the yamin al-ghamus (the false oath that plunges its swearer into sin), especially given their cursed state. We seek refuge with Allah from that [[In M: "We seek refuge with Allah from that."]]. When they met the believers, they said, "We believe," and when they came to the Messenger, they swore by Allah [to him] [[Addition from M.]] that they were believers, while knowing that they were lying in what they swore, because they did not believe in the truth of what they said, even if it happened to correspond with reality. For this reason Allah testified to their lying in their oaths and in their testimony concerning them.

Then He says: ﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾, meaning Allah has readied for them, for this conduct, a painful punishment for their evil deeds, namely their allegiance to the disbelievers and their advising them, and their enmity toward the believers and their deceiving them. For this reason Allah says: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and averted [people] from the way of Allah﴾, meaning they displayed faith and concealed disbelief, and they protected themselves with false oaths. Many who did not know the reality of their situation thought them truthful and were deceived by them, and thus some people were turned away from the way of Allah. ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾, meaning in return for their degrading use of the name of the Great Allah in false oaths that they broke.

Then He says: ﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah at all﴾, meaning these will not avert from them any punishment [[In M: "the punishment of Allah."]] when it comes to them. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

Then He says: ﴿The Day when Allah will resurrect them all﴾, meaning He will gather them on the Day of Resurrection, all of them, leaving none of them behind. ﴿And they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something﴾, meaning they will swear by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that they were upon guidance and uprightness, just as they used to swear to people in this world. This is because whoever lives upon something dies upon it and is resurrected upon it, and they believe that this will benefit them with Allah as it benefited them with people, so that the outward rulings apply to them. For this reason He says: ﴿And they think that they are upon something﴾, meaning their oath to their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, is [based on that belief].

Then He says, rebuking them for their assumption: ﴿Unquestionably, they are the liars﴾, thereby emphasizing the report about them with the word "liars."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Ibn Nufayl narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from [[In M: "Narrated to us."]] Simak ibn Harb, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me that Ibn Abbas narrated to him that the Prophet ﷺ was in the shade of one of his chambers, and with him were some Muslims, while the shade was receding from them. He said: "There will come to you a man who looks through the eyes of a devil. So when he comes to you, do not speak to him." Then a blue-eyed man came, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and spoke with him, saying: "Why do you revile me, you and so-and-so and so-and-so?" — a group whom he named. He said: So the man went and summoned them, and they swore to him and made excuses to him. He said: Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, they are the liars.﴾

This is how Ahmad narrated it through two routes from Simak, with the same chain [[Al-Musnad (1/240).]]. Al-Tabari narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Simak, with similar wording [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/17).]]. He also narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Simak, with similar wording. Its chain is good, but they did not record it.

The condition of these people is as Allah described the polytheists, when He says: ﴿Then their trial will not be except that they say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." Look how they lie against themselves, and what they used to invent has vanished from them﴾ [Al-An'am 6:23–24].

Then He says: ﴿Satan has gained mastery over them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning Satan has taken control of their hearts until he has made them forget to remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is what he does to whomever he gains control over. For this reason Abu Dawud said:

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, al-Sa'ib ibn Hubaysh narrated to us, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah al-Ya'muri, from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "There are no three in a village or in the desert in whom the prayer is not established, except that Satan has gained mastery over them. So keep to the congregation, for the wolf devours only the one that strays." Za'idah said: al-Sa'ib said: meaning the prayer in congregation [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 547.]].

Then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those are the party of Satan﴾, meaning those over whom Satan has gained mastery, so that he has made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Then He says: ﴿Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers.﴾

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, reporting about the disbelievers who oppose and defy Allah and His Messenger, meaning those who are in one boundary while the Sharia is in another boundary; that is, they stray from the truth and oppose it. They are on one side and guidance is on another side. ﴿Those are among the most humiliated﴾, that is, among the wretched, distanced and driven away from what is right, the most humiliated in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers."﴾ That is, He has judged and decreed in His Book beforehand, and in His decree which cannot be opposed, prevented or changed, that victory belongs to Him, to His Book, to His messengers and to His believing servants in this world and the Hereafter, and that the final outcome is for the God-fearing. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand, the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers. And for them is the curse, and for them is the evil home﴾ [Ghafir: 51-52]. And here He said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might."﴾ That is, the Powerful, the Mighty, has decreed that He is the one who overcomes His enemies. This is a firm decree and a settled matter: that the final outcome and victory are for the believers in this world and the Hereafter.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day maintaining friendship with those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers or their kinsmen﴾. That is, they do not show affection to those who oppose Allah, even if they are among their closest relatives, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers. And whoever does that has nothing with Allah, except when taking precaution against them in prudence. And Allah warns you of Himself﴾ [Al 'Imran: 28], and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kinsmen, the wealth you have acquired, the commerce of which you fear a decline, and the dwellings with which you are pleased are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait until Allah brings His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people"﴾ [At-Tawbah: 24].

Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz and others said: This verse, ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ to its end, was revealed concerning Abu 'Ubaydah 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Jarrah, when he killed his father on the day of Badr. For this reason 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said when the matter was made a consultation (shura) among those six after him, may Allah be pleased with them: "If Abu 'Ubaydah were alive, I would have appointed him as successor."

It was also said concerning His saying: ﴿even if they were their fathers﴾, it was revealed about Abu 'Ubaydah who killed his father on the day of Badr; ﴿or their sons﴾ concerning as-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), who intended on that day to kill his son 'Abd al-Rahman; ﴿or their brothers﴾ concerning Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, who killed his brother 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr that day; ﴿or their kinsmen﴾ concerning 'Umar, who killed a relative of his that day as well; and concerning Hamzah, 'Ali and 'Ubaydah ibn al-Harith, who killed 'Utbah, Shaybah and al-Walid ibn 'Utbah that day. And Allah knows best.

I say: Of this kind is what happened when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted the Muslims about the captives of Badr. As-Siddiq advised that ransom be accepted, so that what is taken from them would be a strength for the Muslims, and they were the paternal cousins and kinsmen, and perhaps Allah would guide them. 'Umar said: "I do not see what you saw, O Messenger of Allah. Would you let me strike so-and-so, a relative of 'Umar, and let 'Ali strike 'Aqil, and let so-and-so strike so-and-so, so that Allah knows that there is no tenderness in our hearts toward the polytheists..." the account in its entirety.
